stories.h: US court rejects bid to question Tinubu in FOIA transparency lawsuit
stories.e: A US federal court declined a transparency activist's request to question President Tinubu and a lobbying firm over alleged cyberattacks on a legal research website, ruling the inquiry was not relevant to the underlying public-records case against the FBI and DEA. The long-running dispute concerns efforts to obtain US records on a 1993 drug investigation and asset forfeiture linked to Tinubu, who has invoked personal-privacy grounds to resist fuller disclosure.

stories.h: Tinubu praises EFCC after FBI commends Nigeria role in international sextortion crackdown
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu commended the anti-graft agency EFCC after the FBI director wrote to the commission acknowledging Nigeria contribution to a cross-border crackdown on sextortion crimes. The exchange highlights growing international cooperation on cybercrime enforcement involving Nigerian agencies. It comes as the EFCC own domestic anti-corruption record continues to face public scrutiny.

stories.h: Tinubu praises EFCC role in extradition of Nigerians wanted in US sextortion case
stories.e: President Tinubu commended the EFCC after the FBI credited the agency with helping extradite two Nigerians accused of running an online sextortion scheme targeting American teenage boys. The suspects, arrested under an operation dubbed Operation Artemis, face US charges including distributing child sexual abuse material and offences tied to the deaths of two teenage victims. Tinubu linked the praise to Nigeria's recent removal from international financial-crime watchlists.

stories.h: FG begins N50,000 monthly cash payment to vulnerable Nigerians under new NERSI scheme
stories.e: The federal government has launched a new cash-relief programme, the National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention, paying N50,000 a month to vulnerable households hit by rising food and living costs. Officials say beneficiaries need not register through agents or pay any fee, and funds will reach bank accounts or mobile wallets after an SMS consent process.

stories.h: FG rolls out N50,000 monthly cash payment for vulnerable Nigerians amid rising cost of living
stories.e: The federal government has begun paying N50,000 a month to vulnerable households, with an official citing global food inflation and the rising cost of essential goods as the reason for the intervention. The scheme adds to existing social-investment programmes meant to cushion citizens from economic hardship. Full details on the number of beneficiaries and the funding source have not yet been disclosed.

stories.h: Atiku accuses INEC of cover-up after commission admits AI-generated images on voter register
stories.e: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused INEC of trying to bury evidence after the commission acknowledged that AI-generated images and other irregularities appear on Nigeria's voter register. He is demanding an independent forensic audit, disclosure of the contractors who handled the register, and prosecution of any officials found to have tampered with it ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.h: Falana: Nigerians must hold state, local governments accountable, not just Abuja
stories.e: Human rights lawyer Femi Falana told a Lagos audience that citizens focus too heavily on the federal government while state and local councils often escape scrutiny over how they spend public funds. Speaking at a screening of a documentary on a local government crisis in Osun State, he urged Nigerians to use the Freedom of Information Act to demand spending records from their councils, arguing that weak grassroots oversight is a bigger driver of Nigeria's development gap than federal mismanagement alone.

stories.h: EFCC recovers and returns N114 million to microfinance bank hit by fraud
stories.e: The EFCC's Benin office handed a N114 million bank draft to a Nigerian microfinance bank after tracing funds stolen through a hacked customer account back to a suspect who has since been arrested. The case, opened after a 2024 petition, shows the agency's recovery process working through to a concrete payout, though other suspects remain at large.

stories.h: Investigation finds $857m in loan-funded Nigerian projects abandoned as Tinubu seeks $21.7bn more
stories.e: A BusinessDay investigation found that several Nigerian infrastructure projects funded by roughly $857 million in prior foreign loans, including a security communications network, a rural telephony scheme and a water-sector reform project, now sit abandoned or non-functional. The findings surfaced days after the Senate began reviewing President Tinubu's request for $21.7 billion in fresh external borrowing, prompting economists to call for project-by-project disclosure and independent audits of how loan funds are spent.

stories.h: Ex-SGF Boss Mustapha Flags Pay Gap: Parastatal Chiefs Earning More Than Ministers Combined
stories.e: Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation Boss Mustapha told a civil service colloquium in Abuja that heads of federal parastatals are paid more than ministers, permanent secretaries and directors put together, calling it an anomaly that invites corruption. He urged the Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission to overhaul public-sector pay structures to reward the officials who actually manage trillion-naira budgets. His remarks add a prominent insider voice to long-running concerns about opaque and lopsided pay across Nigeria's civil service.

stories.h: FEC approves ₦631.3bn for nine road projects nationwide
stories.e: The Federal Executive Council, chaired by President Tinubu, approved roughly ₦631.3 billion for nine road projects across the country, including a ₦209 billion reconstruction of the Ado-Ilawe-Ikole road in Ekiti and a ₦167 billion rebuild of the Etuke-Okeni-Ankpa-Otopa road in Kogi. Works Minister David Umahi announced the approvals, which also cover remedial work on the East-West Road and a Sokoto-Illela rehabilitation. The council publicly named only seven of the nine funded projects.

stories.h: EFCC Hands Over N1.05bn to 659 Sacked Adamawa Teachers
stories.e: The EFCC's Gombe zonal office handed over roughly N1.05 billion to 659 teachers the Adamawa State government controversially dismissed in 2014, after a 2018 labour court ruling in their favour went largely unpaid for years. The commission said it stepped in after flagging a risk that funds owed to the teachers could be diverted. The payout follows a 2024 petition and years of legal wrangling over the outstanding balance.

stories.h: Court jails FCDA official seven years for defrauding land buyer
stories.e: A Federal Capital Territory High Court in Abuja convicted Kinsley Eselebor, a Federal Capital Development Authority staff member, on five fraud counts brought by the EFCC. He sold two plots of land in Kubwa to a businessman using forged ownership documents despite holding no valid title, and was sentenced to seven years with no option of a fine.

stories.h: ICPC re-arraigns fake 'Presidential Council' DG Adeniyi Adeyemi for forgery, fraud
stories.e: Nigeria's anti-graft agency, the ICPC, has filed fresh forgery and fraud charges against Adeniyi Adeyemi, who had posed as director-general of a non-existent 'Presidential Council' agency. The re-arraignment follows earlier charges and reflects the commission's push to hold the impersonator accountable for using a fabricated government title.

stories.h: Tinubu's $21.7bn loan plan puts lawmakers' independence to the test
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has sent the National Assembly a fresh request to borrow $21.67 billion from external lenders, adding to Nigeria's debt-service burden. Because lawmakers have approved every loan request submitted since 2023, this ask is being framed as a test of whether the legislature will exercise real oversight or simply rubber-stamp it.

stories.h: Enugu clerics disown APC campaign list, demand removal of their names
stories.e: The Catholic Diocese of Enugu and the Enugu chapter of the Christian Association of Nigeria say the ruling APC added a bishop and other clergy to a faith-based campaign group for the state governorship race without their consent. Church officials called the move unauthorised and warned of legal action unless their names are withdrawn, saying the listing falsely implies a partisan endorsement by institutions that are meant to stay neutral in politics.

stories.h: Obasanjo warns Tinubu's borrowing spree could harm future generations of Nigerians
stories.e: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo publicly criticised the Tinubu government's growing reliance on domestic and foreign loans, rejecting the president's comparison of debt to a harmless condition as nonsense. His remarks come as Tinubu seeks National Assembly approval for roughly $20.5 billion and 1.05 billion euros in fresh external borrowing, adding to mounting opposition concern over Nigeria's debt trajectory ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.h: Atiku presses INEC on voter register as Tinubu defends fresh $20.5bn borrowing plan
stories.e: In a roundup of Friday political developments, Atiku Abubakar and the NDC pushed the electoral commission to correct irregularities in the roughly 103-million-strong voters register before next year election, while INEC pledged fixes ahead of certification. Separately, President Tinubu defended his request to the National Assembly for about $20.5 billion and over one billion euros in fresh external loans, arguing the funds are needed for development projects. Both developments reflect mounting pre-election tension over electoral transparency and the administration debt strategy.

stories.h: Lagos deputy governor Hamzat unveils 100-point manifesto in 2027 governorship bid
stories.e: Lagos Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, the APC's candidate for the 2027 governorship race, launched a 100-point manifesto pledging a new child protection and nutrition agency, an independently audited state wealth fund, and service charters requiring government offices to resolve complaints within set deadlines. He said 87 of the pledges are within the state's direct power, while the rest depend on cooperation from the federal government and courts.

stories.h: Tinubu travels to Saudi Arabia for Umrah as aide denies health concerns
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu left Nigeria for Saudi Arabia to perform the Umrah pilgrimage, with his media team describing the trip as spiritual rather than medical after online speculation about his health. The visit comes as Nigeria heads toward January 2027 general elections, with insecurity and the economy expected to dominate campaigning against challengers Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi.

stories.h: INEC approves 41 petitions, rejects 28 over 2027 governorship candidate list
stories.e: INEC says it approved 41 petitions and rejected 28 others filed by parties disputing the exclusion of candidates from its final 2027 governorship list. The ruling follows weeks of complaints from parties including the PDP and NNPP after the commission dropped several candidates, citing a September Supreme Court ruling on party membership-register compliance.

stories.h: PDP insists Sandy Onor remains its 2027 presidential candidate despite backing Tinubu
stories.e: A PDP state chairman says the party's own candidate, Sandy Onor, is still in the 2027 race even though the party has thrown its weight behind President Tinubu through a cross-party Rainbow Coalition. He described the arrangement as a coalition rather than a merger, with member parties free to keep their own candidates for other positions.

stories.h: Obasanjo slams Tinubu's borrowing as public debt hits N166.79 trillion
stories.e: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo publicly rejected President Tinubu's defence of his borrowing policy, warning that mounting debt threatens future generations of Nigerians. His remarks, made at a public forum in Abeokuta, come as the Debt Management Office reports public debt has nearly doubled to N166.79 trillion since mid-2023.

stories.h: 14 Arrested After Thugs Attack APC Supporters Heading to Tinubu-Dikko Campaign Rally in Katsina
stories.e: Katsina police say suspected political thugs armed with stones and knives ambushed vehicles carrying APC supporters to a campaign flag-off event in Funtua, injuring at least one passenger and damaging several cars. Fourteen suspects, including a minor, have been arrested, while police say the hunt for others continues. The attack underscores rising concerns about political violence as campaigning intensifies ahead of Nigeria's 2027 elections.

stories.h: Tinubu appoints six executive directors for petroleum regulator NMDPRA
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu asked the Senate to confirm six executive directors for the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, reappointing three incumbents and naming three new nominees to oversee areas such as hydrocarbon processing and economic regulation. The five-year appointments come as a separate Senate panel is questioning NMDPRA and NNPC over discrepancies in petrol import records.

stories.h: Court strips Uzodimma of APC Imo West senate ticket, hands it to Okorocha
stories.e: A Federal High Court judge in Abuja ruled that Rochas Okorocha, not sitting Imo governor Hope Uzodimma, actually won the APC's May 18 Imo West senatorial primary, and ordered INEC to recognise Okorocha as the party's candidate for 2027. The two camps had disputed the primary's vote count, and Uzodimma is expected to challenge the ruling on appeal.

stories.h: Court sacks Uzodimma as APC's Imo West senatorial candidate, orders INEC to recognise Okorocha
stories.e: A court has stripped Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma of recognition as the APC's candidate for the Imo West senatorial seat, ruling that Rochas Okorocha should instead be recognised by INEC. The APC has pushed back, insisting Uzodimma remains its authentic candidate, setting up a fresh legal and political battle ahead of 2027.

stories.h: Akpabio says 30 states have endorsed constitutional amendment to create state police
stories.e: Senate President Godswill Akpabio says 30 state Houses of Assembly have now backed the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police forces, clearing the two-thirds threshold needed for the reform to proceed. The amendment, pushed as a response to Nigeria's worsening insecurity, had already passed both chambers of the National Assembly and was sent to the states for concurrence.

stories.h: Tinubu to send 2027 budget to lawmakers before year's end, minister says
stories.e: Minister of State for Budget Doris Uzoka-Anite said after a Federal Executive Council meeting that the 2027 Appropriation Bill is being finalised and should reach the National Assembly before December 31, 2026. No exact presentation date was given, and the timeline runs alongside preparations for Nigeria's 2027 general elections.

stories.h: Senate Leader Vows National Assembly Will Finalise State Police Law by December
stories.e: Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele said both chambers of the National Assembly aim to complete all remaining steps toward establishing state police forces by December, including reviewing state legislature resolutions and forwarding the amendment for presidential assent. Around 30 of Nigeria's 36 state assemblies have already approved the constitutional amendment, clearing the required two-thirds threshold. Under the plan, state police would operate alongside federal police, with governors appointing commissioners subject to state assembly confirmation.

stories.h: OPay pulls planned $304m New York IPO after foreign regulatory inquiry
stories.e: Nigerian fintech giant OPay withdrew its planned US stock market listing, which would have raised around $304 million at a valuation above $4 billion, after disclosing an unnamed foreign regulatory inquiry. The company said the probe involves a jurisdiction immaterial to its core operations and insisted it would not affect services for its Nigerian customers. The reversal comes only weeks after OPay secured approval for a separate listing on the Nigerian Exchange.

stories.h: BUA Foods' nine-month profit climbs to N450.5bn despite falling revenue
stories.e: BUA Foods reported an 11% rise in nine-month net profit to N450.5 billion even as turnover fell by about 19% amid weaker demand for its flour and sugar products. The company said sharp cuts in raw-material and administrative costs helped push its EBITDA margin above 43%, up from roughly 31% a year earlier.

stories.h: OPay pulls $304 million NYSE listing hours after pricing shares
stories.e: SoftBank-backed fintech OPay withdrew its planned $304 million US stock listing shortly after pricing shares at $19 each, just before trading was due to begin on the NYSE. The company said the move followed an inquiry from a regulator in a foreign jurisdiction it described as immaterial to its core business, and that it expects the matter to be resolved soon. The abrupt reversal raises questions about how ready Nigerian fintechs are for the scrutiny of US capital markets.

stories.h: Dangote Cement nine-month profit jumps 31% as revenue hits N3.8 trillion
stories.e: Dangote Cement posted a 31% rise in nine-month after-tax profit to roughly N975 billion, with revenue climbing to about N3.8 trillion, helped by lower finance costs and reduced foreign exchange losses. The results, covering the period through September 2026, lifted the companys share price on the Nigerian Exchange.

stories.h: Nigerian fintech OPay lists on NYSE, raises $304 million in IPO at over $4 billion valuation
stories.e: OPay began trading on the New York Stock Exchange, selling 16 million depositary shares at $19 apiece to raise roughly $304 million and value the Lagos-founded fintech at more than $4 billion. The listing marks one of the largest-ever US market debuts for an African-founded technology company.

stories.h: 23 Nigerian States Report 27% Jump in Tax Revenue Under New Tax Act
stories.e: The Joint Revenue Board says 23 states that submitted returns collected about N2.2 trillion in tax revenue in the first half of 2026, a 27% rise from the same period last year, which it credits partly to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. The new law exempts the first N800,000 of annual income and caps the top personal income tax rate at 25%, with officials saying most low earners in these states now pay less or nothing. Thirteen states have yet to adopt the board's harmonised tax law, leaving a patchwork of rules across the country.

stories.h: Nigerian Stock Market Hits Record N164.97tn as Dangote Cement Leads Rally
stories.e: Nigeria's equities market closed at a fresh all-time high of N164.97 trillion, adding roughly N779 billion in a single session as the All-Share Index climbed to a record 254,083 points. Dangote Cement, the exchange's largest listed company, drove the gain with a near-6% share price jump, while banking stocks dragged on the index after First HoldCo tumbled 10%. The milestone extends a rally that had already set a previous record just two days earlier.

stories.h: TUC rejects FG's ₦70,000 transport allowance, demands ₦300,000 minimum wage instead
stories.e: The Trade Union Congress has rejected the federal government's proposed six-month ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for public servants as inadequate temporary relief, arguing the government could instead raise the minimum wage to ₦300,000 without waiting for a formal review. The union said trust had eroded because an October 2023 wage award to workers was never fully paid.

stories.h: Lagos unveils 2052 growth plan, targets $1 trillion economy
stories.e: Lagos State has unveiled a long-term development blueprint targeting a one-trillion-dollar economy by 2052, outlining investment priorities across infrastructure, technology and trade. The plan reflects the state government's effort to position Lagos as a global economic hub over the coming decades.

stories.h: South Africa widens economic lead over Nigeria after GDP revision
stories.e: A rebasing of South Africa's national accounts has widened its lead over Nigeria as Africa's largest economy, with Statistics South Africa raising its 2025 nominal GDP estimate to roughly $483 billion against Nigeria's about $328 billion. Economists note the shift partly reflects naira depreciation and differing measurement methods rather than a straightforward change in real output.

stories.h: 21 States Adopt Harmonised Tax Law, Board Bans Cash Roadblocks for Road Tax
stories.e: Nigeria's Joint Revenue Board said 21 states have now passed a model law harmonising more than 100 separate state and local taxes into a single simplified structure, part of the rollout of the federal Tax Acts that took effect this year. The board also announced a ban on collecting road tax at checkpoints and said it would work with police to enforce it, aiming to end a longstanding source of extortion and multiple taxation for businesses and commuters. Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele said the reform is built around clarity, fairness and administrative certainty.

stories.h: FG to pay workers N70,000 monthly transport support for six months
stories.e: The Federal Ministry of Labour reached a deal with the Nigeria Labour Congress to pay government workers a N70,000 monthly transport allowance for six months starting November, alongside overdue allowances and health workers' arrears, averting threatened strike action. The agreement followed collapsed talks on October 22 amid union pressure over high living costs and fuel prices.

stories.h: TUC Rejects FG's N70,000 Transport Allowance, Demands Immediate Salary Increase
stories.e: The Trade Union Congress has rejected the federal government's offer of a N70,000 transport allowance for workers, calling instead for an outright salary increase and implementation of an earlier agreement with health workers. The pushback came a day after the government announced the allowance, signalling continued friction over worker pay.

stories.h: TUC rejects FG's ₦70,000 transport allowance, demands outright pay rise
stories.e: Labour union TUC rejected a Federal Government offer of a ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance plus backdated arrears, calling it a stopgap rather than the real wage increase workers need to cope with living costs. The union noted that the 2023 wage award itself was never fully implemented, with most states and the informal sector still ignoring it, and warned against letting minimum-wage talks delay action. The rejection came two days after government and the NLC reached a separate conciliation agreement on the allowance.

stories.h: 21 states adopt harmonised tax law to end multiple taxation
stories.e: Twenty-one Nigerian states have now adopted a harmonised tax law designed to consolidate the patchwork of state levies, charges and informal roadblock taxes that businesses have long blamed for raising operating costs. The law bans practices like cash tax collection and unauthorised stickers or emblems, and sets penalties for violations, aiming to make the sub-national tax environment more predictable for investors. The rollout follows years of complaints from manufacturers and traders about overlapping, sometimes illegal levies across state lines.

stories.h: OPay pulls $304m NYSE listing days after pricing shares, cites foreign regulatory probe
stories.e: Nigerian-founded fintech OPay abruptly terminated its planned New York Stock Exchange listing just two days after signing its underwriting agreement, citing an unspecified regulatory inquiry in a foreign jurisdiction it called immaterial to its core business. The $304 million offering had valued the SoftBank-backed company at more than $4 billion, and OPay says normal operations in Nigeria and other markets will continue while it works to resolve the issue.

stories.h: UBA Becomes First Nigerian Bank to Enable Google Pay for Visa, Mastercard Customers
stories.e: United Bank for Africa says it is the first bank in Nigeria to switch on Google Pay for eligible Visa and Mastercard holders, letting customers tap their phones to pay instead of carrying a physical card. The rollout follows Google Wallet's broader launch in Nigeria and relies on tokenisation infrastructure built with card networks and payment processors. It is part of a wider push by Nigerian banks to modernise digital payments as contactless transactions gain traction.

stories.h: DMO rejects N1.84 trillion in bids at latest Treasury bills auction
stories.e: Nigeria's Debt Management Office allotted just N71.16 billion out of nearly N1.9 trillion in bids at its October 28 Treasury bills auction, rejecting the vast majority of investor demand for the second straight sale. The one-year stop rate edged down to 15.80%, even as banking-system liquidity rose sharply on the maturity of prior central bank operations.

stories.h: Only 59% of Nigerian banks and fintechs ready for CBN's January 2027 data localisation deadline
stories.e: A NITDA survey conducted October 13-27 found that just 26 of 44 responding financial institutions had completed or were likely to complete the steps needed to comply with the CBN's new rule requiring payment data generated in Nigeria to be stored on local servers. Fifteen institutions said compliance by the January 1, 2027 deadline was unlikely, and 22 had not yet begun implementation work such as budgeting and system migration.

stories.h: DMO rejects N1.84 trillion bids, pushes T-bill rates lower
stories.e: The Debt Management Office rejected N1.84 trillion worth of bids at its latest Treasury bills auction, a move that pushed yields lower as the government manages domestic borrowing costs. The rejection reflects the DMO's strategy of resisting investor demands for higher returns even amid strong demand for short-term government debt.

stories.h: Fidelity Bank Plc redeems $400 million Eurobond at maturity
stories.e: Fidelity Bank has fully repaid a $400 million Eurobond on its maturity date, a transaction seen as a signal of the lender's financial strength and continued access to international capital markets. The repayment comes as Nigerian banks navigate a tighter global funding environment.

stories.h: Nigeria posts Africa's sharpest inflation drop as naira stability aids disinflation
stories.e: Nigeria's headline inflation eased to 14.63% in September from 15.39% in August, its fourth straight monthly decline and the lowest rate since January 2025, giving it the steepest annual drop among Africa's ten largest economies. Analysts linked the slowdown to a more stable naira, among the best-performing African currencies this year, which has eased imported-inflation pressure and supported the central bank's recent 350-basis-point rate cut. Food inflation, however, stayed stubbornly high near 19.6%, showing price relief has not reached everyday staples.

stories.h: CBN offers N800bn in Treasury bills as bank deposits near N7trn
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria is auctioning N800 billion in Treasury bills this week, well above the N130.72 billion actually maturing, as banks' deposits at the CBN's standing facility approach N7 trillion. The outsized offer will test whether ample banking-system liquidity translates into strong demand without forcing yields higher, after a recent auction saw roughly three-quarters of bids rejected.

stories.h: NCGC Guarantees N64.13bn in Loans to Businesses, Individuals
stories.e: The National Credit Guarantee Company says it has backed loans worth N64.13 billion to small businesses and individuals, using a partial-guarantee model to unlock financing that commercial banks might otherwise withhold. The disbursement is part of a wider government push to widen access to credit for underserved borrowers.

stories.h: Nigerian banks, Interswitch roll out tokenised card payments to curb fraud
stories.e: Major Nigerian banks and payments firm Interswitch are rolling out tokenised card payments, which swap a customer's card number for a disposable digital identifier so stolen data cannot be reused by fraudsters. Executives say the shift also reflects more Nigerians paying by phone rather than physical card, and plan to extend the technology to more merchants.

stories.h: Nigerian bank stocks rally 79% year-to-date even as valuation discounts persist
stories.e: Nigerian bank stocks have surged as much as 79% so far this year on falling interest rates and stronger earnings, though analysts say many lenders still trade at steep discounts to book value. The rally follows the central bank's shift toward looser monetary policy and improved governance at some of the country's largest banks.

stories.h: Nigerian Stock Market Hits Record N163.1 Trillion Capitalisation
stories.e: The Nigerian Exchange's total equity market capitalisation climbed to an all-time high of about N163.1 trillion, driven by a sustained rally across banking and industrial stocks. Analysts tie the surge partly to the Central Bank's recent interest-rate cuts, which have pushed investors toward equities in search of higher returns. The rally has also coincided with a wave of corporate earnings reports showing improved profitability for several listed companies.

stories.h: UBA, Access, First HoldCo still barred from paying dividends under CBN restrictions
stories.e: Three of Nigeria's largest banks, UBA, Access Holdings and First HoldCo, remain unable to pay dividends under a CBN directive restricting payouts for lenders with unresolved loan-forbearance exposures, despite all three staying profitable in 2025. The restriction, in place since mid-2025, requires banks to make adequate loss provisions and meet lending limits before resuming dividends, bonuses or new offshore investments. None of the three banks has confirmed the central bank has cleared them to resume payouts.

stories.h: CBN Grants JPMorgan Approval-in-Principle to Launch Merchant Bank in Nigeria
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria has given JPMorgan approval-in-principle to establish a merchant bank, naming Adedapo Olagunju as managing director alongside three non-executive directors. The approval is only the first licensing stage, with JPMorgan still needing incorporation and further regulatory sign-off before operations can begin, likely by year-end or early 2027. The bank previously deposited ₦50 billion with the CBN as part of its capital requirement under Nigeria's recapitalisation framework.

stories.h: Naira Posts Sharpest One-Day Drop in 18 Months, Slips to Around N1,365/$
stories.e: The naira recorded its steepest single-day fall in roughly a year and a half, slipping to about N1,365 to the dollar on the official market, according to Nairametrics. The drop reverses recent gains and renews pressure on households already squeezed by high food and transport costs. Markets will be watching whether the central bank responds with fresh interventions in the coming days.

stories.h: Nigeria's top cement makers post combined N1.71trn profit in nine months
stories.e: Nigeria's three major cement producers posted a combined 37.8% rise in nine-month profit to N1.71 trillion, driven largely by stronger margins and cost efficiencies rather than higher sales volumes. The results underline the sector's continued profitability even as high construction costs remain a strain on ordinary Nigerians.

stories.h: Manufacturers face fresh squeeze on rising diesel prices
stories.e: Nigerian manufacturers are facing renewed cost pressure as diesel prices climb again, squeezing already thin margins for firms that rely on generators amid unreliable grid electricity. Industry groups warn the latest increase could further erode the sector's competitiveness and slow production.

stories.h: Manufacturers spent ₦1.35trn on alternative power in 2025 as sector shed nearly 19,000 jobs
stories.e: Manufacturers Association of Nigeria data presented at an industry AGM shows local manufacturers spent an estimated ₦1.35 trillion on alternative power in 2025, a 23% jump from the prior year, while the sector lost 18,935 jobs in the first half of 2025 alone, nearly double the losses recorded a year earlier. The figures point to unreliable grid supply, with delivered power still far below estimated industrial demand despite rising installed capacity.

stories.h: MAN: manufacturers still borrowing at 30% despite bank recapitalisation
stories.e: The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria says its members are still borrowing at around 30% interest even after banks completed a recapitalisation exercise meant to expand lending, with association president Ifeanyi Okoye contrasting this with Chinese manufacturers who can access credit as cheap as 3%. Speaking at the Nigerian Economic Summit, he said only token rate cuts have reached manufacturers, leaving them at a cost disadvantage against foreign competitors.

stories.h: Nigeria to begin mass production of military munitions within a year, says defence minister
stories.e: Defence Minister Christopher Musa told delegates at Nigeria first Africa International Defence Exhibition in Lagos that local production of defence hardware for domestic use and export to other African countries will start within a year. The head of the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria pledged to expand production capacity, with the event drawing officials from more than 20 African countries.

stories.h: Manufacturers cut forex demand by $1bn through local sourcing
stories.e: Nigerian manufacturers reduced their foreign exchange needs by roughly $1 billion in the first half of 2026 as more firms source raw materials locally instead of importing them, according to new industry data. The shift toward backward integration reflects a wider push by producers to cut costs amid ongoing currency pressures.

stories.h: Manufacturers Association to Launch Industrial Energy Cost Reduction Programme in November
stories.e: The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria said it will roll out a new programme next month aimed at helping member companies cut their energy costs, which have become one of the biggest drags on local production. The initiative responds to years of complaints from manufacturers about high electricity tariffs and unreliable power supply squeezing already-thin margins. Details on specific cost-saving measures are expected to be unveiled closer to the launch date.

stories.h: $5bn Ajaokuta steel revival still stalled by power and supply problems
stories.e: A fresh push to revive the long-dormant, $5 billion Ajaokuta Steel Complex is running into the same obstacles that have stalled the plant for decades, including unreliable power supply and shortages of raw materials, according to BusinessDay. The report underscores how one of Nigeria's biggest unfinished public infrastructure investments remains far from generating the industrial jobs and output officials have long promised.

stories.h: Dangote plans additional $1.5bn expansion of Kenya Pipeline network
stories.e: Aliko Dangote plans to invest an additional $1.5 billion to expand Kenya Pipeline Company's network, days after buying a 25% stake in the state-linked firm through a roughly $327 million share purchase on the Nairobi Securities Exchange. The move builds on Dangote's wider push into East African energy infrastructure, which also includes a planned $16 billion refinery in Lamu.

stories.h: Business chamber says Nigeria needs more manufacturing investment to reach $1trn economy
stories.e: A deputy president of the Abuja Chamber of Commerce and Industry told a business lecture in Abuja that Nigeria must channel far more capital into manufacturing and fix unreliable electricity supply to convert recent macroeconomic gains into real industrial growth. He noted manufacturing attracted only a small fraction of foreign direct investment in early 2026, despite government ambitions for a trillion-dollar economy.

stories.h: Chemical Engineers Seek Private Control of Moribund Refineries
stories.e: The Nigerian Society of Chemical Engineers has called on the Federal Government to privatise the country's state-owned refineries in Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna through a transparent, time-bound competitive process, rather than continuing to fund repeated failed rehabilitation efforts. The group's president proposed a 22-month transition plan covering asset assessment, investor bidding and ownership transfer, with government retaining only a minority stake. The proposal responds to more than two decades of costly, unsuccessful attempts to revive the plants.

stories.h: Manufacturing Activity Falls 10 Percent as Cement Sector Slides Into Contraction
stories.e: The Nigerian Economic Summit Group's Business Confidence Monitor shows manufacturing activity dropped roughly 10 percent in September, driven largely by a contraction in cement production alongside declines in chemicals, plastics, steel and auto assembly. NESG attributes the slowdown to persistent energy shortages, raw-material shortages, high rents and tight credit, which it says are raising production costs and discouraging new industrial investment.

stories.h: CBN data show bank lending to manufacturers fell 26.8% to N5.19 trillion
stories.e: Fresh Central Bank data show commercial bank credit flowing to Nigerian manufacturers dropped by 26.8% to N5.19 trillion, raising concerns about financing conditions for the real sector. The decline comes despite government rhetoric about boosting industrial output and local production.

stories.h: Manufacturing investment jumps 102% on backward-integration push
stories.e: Investment in Nigerian manufacturing assets roughly doubled in 2025, rising about 102% to near N1.33 trillion, driven largely by companies building local supply chains instead of relying on imported inputs. The surge suggests some industrial firms are betting on long-term local production despite tough financing conditions.

stories.h: Decades-stalled Katsina wind farm exposes Nigeria's struggle to build a renewable energy industry
stories.e: A long-stalled 10-megawatt wind farm in Katsina State, first begun in 2005 and still incomplete after multiple contractors and conflicting progress reports, illustrates the broader obstacles facing Nigeria's renewable energy push, according to a new investigation. Experts cite weak policy certainty, financing gaps and grid constraints as recurring barriers, contrasting Nigeria's slow progress with Egypt's faster shift to solar power. Katsina State is now trying to revive the project by pairing it with a new solar plant.

stories.h: Security agencies rescue three Zamfara clerics kidnapped en route to prayer session for Tinubu
stories.e: Nigeria's national security office and the DSS freed three clergymen who were abducted in Zamfara State while travelling to a prayer session organised in support of President Tinubu. Reports indicate operations are continuing to secure the release of other captives still being held from the same incident. The abduction underscores the persistent insecurity facing religious leaders and ordinary civilians in parts of northern Nigeria.

stories.h: Panel finds NSCDC officers negligent in deaths of 33 detainees, including 14 children, in Niger State
stories.e: A federal investigative panel examining the deaths of 33 people, including 14 children, held in a civil defence detention cell in Minna found officers authorised an unapproved raid, crammed dozens of detainees into one cell, and ignored warnings and cries for help over several hours. The panel recommended that the suspended commandant and several colleagues be dismissed and criminally prosecuted for offences including murder and torture, with the case now referred to the Attorney-General.

stories.h: El-Rufai marks 256th day in detention, appeals to Trump and Macron for a fair trial
stories.e: Former Kaduna governor Nasir El-Rufai marked his 256th day in detention by publicly appealing to international leaders and rights bodies, including the UN and Amnesty International, saying a fair trial is not an act of mercy. He has been held since February 2026 after honouring an EFCC invitation, and his family has long disputed the legality of the ICPC detention order.

stories.h: Panel recommends N1.4bn compensation, scholarships for victims of Niger NSCDC custodial deaths
stories.e: An independent panel probing the September deaths of 33 detainees, including children, in NSCDC custody in Niger State has recommended about N1.4 billion in compensation for bereaved families and survivors, plus full scholarships for victims children and funded medical and psychosocial care for survivors. The panel also called for the dismissal of culpable officers and a formal government apology, concluding the deaths were preventable and stemmed from an unauthorized raid and an overcrowded cell.

stories.h: Months On, Families of 78 Abducted Borno Schoolchildren Still Await Tinubu's Intervention
stories.e: Parents from Askira/Uba in Borno State say 78 children and a teacher, abducted in two separate attacks in May and during NECO exams in June, remain in captivity, with no confirmed word on whether President Tinubu has even been briefed on their case. The community says letters to the National Security Adviser have gone unanswered and attempts to meet National Assembly leaders have failed, even as the state government's early assurances of a swift return have not materialised. Their renewed appeal comes as advocacy groups point to the successful rescue of children abducted in Oyo State as proof that faster action is possible.

stories.h: Gunmen kill four in Plateau community despite state-imposed curfew
stories.e: Suspected gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community in Barkin Ladi council area of Plateau State around 8pm, killing at least four people even though a dusk-to-dawn curfew was in force. A resident said authorities had been warned of a possible attack a day earlier, and a local youth group is demanding faster security response to early warnings.

stories.h: Detainees drank urine and sweat before 33 died in NSCDC Niger cell, probe finds
stories.e: An independent investigation into the deaths of 33 detainees held by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in Niger State found that officers packed around 50 people, including children, into a tiny, poorly ventilated cell with no running water, ignoring warnings that overcrowding could cause suffocation. The panel rejected the agency's earlier claim that a disease outbreak was to blame and recommended prosecuting the officers involved.

stories.h: NSCDC suspends officer over misuse of firearm in Abuja market
stories.e: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps has suspended one of its officers after he was filmed misusing a firearm at a market in Abuja, alarming traders and shoppers nearby. The agency says the officer will face internal disciplinary proceedings while the matter is investigated.

stories.h: Police probe officer filmed assaulting man in Imo
stories.e: Nigeria's police authorities say they are investigating an officer captured on video assaulting a man in Imo State, after the footage circulated widely online and sparked public outrage. The case adds to a string of recent incidents raising questions about accountability for police misconduct.

stories.h: 20 years after launch, health insurance still covers less than 10% of Nigerians
stories.e: Two decades after Nigeria launched its national health insurance scheme, officials say coverage still reaches less than 10% of the population, with the National Health Insurance Authority reporting about 23 million enrollees out of an estimated 244 million people. The figures, presented at a health conference in Abuja, show enrollment growing but still far short of the universal coverage the scheme was designed to deliver.

stories.h: Reps Demand Security and Humanitarian Relief After Gunmen Kill Dozens in Taraba Market Attack
stories.e: Lawmakers in the House of Representatives raised an urgent motion over an October 23 attack on Binnari market in Taraba State, where gunmen reportedly came from forested areas spanning Plateau and Bauchi states and killed dozens of traders and residents, with some victims drowning as they fled into a river. The House called for completion of an abandoned road project, better security coordination between the three states, and emergency relief, including food and shelter, for survivors. A second raid on a neighbouring community days later saw attackers loot food and seize vehicles, deepening fears about the region's worsening security situation.

stories.h: Africa CDC Warns Continent 'Not Winning' Ebola Fight as Cases Top 10,000, Nigeria Confirms One Case
stories.e: Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya told an emergency meeting of health ministers that the continent is not yet winning its fight against Ebola, as WHO figures put the outbreak at over 10,000 cases and nearly 4,900 deaths, mostly in the DR Congo. Nigeria's health minister said genomic sequencing linked the country's single imported case, now evacuated to Switzerland, closely to the strain found in Kenya, though he cautioned this does not confirm a direct link between the two. The NCDC says it is still tracing dozens of contacts of the Nigerian patient as authorities step up surveillance nationwide.

stories.h: Katsina Cleric and Associate Shot Dead Outside Home, Investigation Ongoing
stories.e: Gunmen on a motorcycle shot dead Islamic scholar Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka and an associate outside his residence in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, in an attack police say happened in the evening hours. An extremist group has claimed responsibility, though police have not independently confirmed the attackers' identity and no arrests have been announced. President Tinubu condemned the killings and ordered a full investigation, underscoring persistent rural security gaps in northern Nigeria.

stories.h: Gunmen kill one, wound pastor in fresh attack on Plateau community
stories.e: Suspected gunmen attacked a farm in Lamor community, Pushit District of Plateau State's Mangu council area, killing a 36-year-old resident and wounding a local pastor, while a 57-year-old man remains missing. Community members linked the attackers to a group blamed for a string of recent assaults across Plateau and renewed calls for security forces to investigate, make arrests and increase their presence in the area. Security officials could not be reached for comment on the incident at the time of reporting.

stories.h: Senate Demands Security Crackdown as Taraba Killings Death Toll Climbs to 80
stories.e: The Senate is calling for an intensified security response in Taraba State after the death toll from recent attacks on communities there climbed sharply, with lawmakers demanding tighter border surveillance and more security camps. The rising casualty figures have drawn fresh scrutiny of the federal response to communal violence in the state.

stories.h: Nigeria, Russia agree to replace 59-year-old aviation agreement
stories.e: Nigeria's aviation minister Festus Keyamo and Russian officials agreed, on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, to renegotiate the countries' 1967 air services pact. Both sides have set up negotiating teams and aim to sign a replacement agreement in Saint Petersburg in April 2027, though no route or airline details have been disclosed yet.

stories.h: Nigeria, Russia agree to renegotiate 59-year-old aviation pact
stories.e: Nigeria's aviation minister Festus Keyamo met Russian officials at the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow and agreed to renegotiate the countries' 1967 bilateral air services agreement, with both sides aiming to finalise a new deal in Saint Petersburg by April 2027. Neither side has yet disclosed what routes or airlines the updated agreement would cover.

stories.h: Russian drone strike kills 14 at Ukraine train station
stories.e: A Russian drone strike on a train station in Ukraine has killed 14 people, in what officials described as a horrific attack on civilian infrastructure. The strike adds to the mounting civilian toll of Russia's continuing war against Ukraine.

stories.h: Nigeria joins 129 other nations at UN in demanding end to US embargo on Cuba
stories.e: Nigeria was among 130 countries that backed a UN General Assembly resolution calling for an end to the decades-old US economic embargo on Cuba, a vote the US and Israel opposed and 25 nations abstained from. Most African states supported the resolution, which has passed annually since 1992 and comes as fresh US sanctions have deepened Cuba's economic strain.

stories.h: Nigeria downgrades delegation to Russia-Africa summit, keeps Tinubu and VP away
stories.e: Nigeria sent only Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Sola Enikanolaiye to the two-day Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, after earlier plans for Vice President Kashim Shettima to lead the delegation were quietly dropped without explanation from the presidency. Analysts link the low-key presence to Nigeria's deepening ties with the United States and the approaching 2027 election campaign.

stories.h: CAR tightens border checks as DR Congo Ebola cases rise
stories.e: The Central African Republic has tightened checks at its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as an Ebola outbreak there continues to spread into new provinces. The heightened screening aims to prevent cross-border transmission as regional health authorities scale up containment efforts.

stories.h: Uganda orders 21-day quarantine for travellers from DR Congo as Ebola spreads
stories.e: Uganda has imposed a mandatory 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo, as health authorities work to contain an Ebola outbreak in the region that has also produced a confirmed case in Nigeria. The measure reflects growing concern across East and West Africa about the virus's spread.

stories.h: DRC Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases, nearly 5,000 deaths, as WHO cites hopeful signs
stories.e: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, now the world's second-deadliest on record, has passed 10,000 confirmed cases and nearly 5,000 deaths, health authorities reported. The WHO's Africa director said rising case numbers reflect a heavy toll but pointed to over 2,600 recoveries and advancing vaccine trials as reasons for cautious optimism, while noting infections linked to the outbreak have already surfaced in Kenya and Nigeria.

stories.h: Ebola cases in DR Congo surpass 10,000 in fastest-growing outbreak on record
stories.e: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has now infected more than 10,000 people, making it the fastest-growing epidemic of the disease that health authorities have tracked. Neighbouring countries including Uganda and Kenya have tightened border and quarantine measures as the virus keeps crossing into other parts of the region.

stories.h: Lula wins historic fourth term as Brazil's president, Bolsonaro refuses to concede
stories.e: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defeated Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil's presidential runoff, winning about 51.8% of the vote to become the first candidate since Brazil's return to democracy to win after trailing in the first round. Bolsonaro has refused to concede and is seeking to have the results annulled, extending political uncertainty in Latin America's largest democracy.

stories.h: Nurse killed, health worker injured in attack on Ebola responders in DRC
stories.e: The World Health Organisation reported that a nurse was killed and another health worker seriously hurt in an attack on an Ebola response team in Bafwasende, eastern DRC. WHO leaders condemned the assault as part of a pattern of violence against health workers during the ongoing outbreak, which has also produced Nigeria's only imported case, a woman evacuated to Switzerland after traveling from Uganda.

stories.h: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil's president, defeating Bolsonaro's son in runoff
stories.e: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has been re-elected Brazil's president for a fourth term, narrowly beating far-right senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed former president, in a runoff held Sunday. Lula took just over 51.7% of the vote, breaking a recent run of right-wing election wins across Latin America, though Bolsonaro has rejected the outcome and says he will seek to have it annulled.

stories.h: WHO Says Nigeria Has No Active Ebola Cases After Patient's Evacuation to Switzerland
stories.e: The World Health Organization's Africa regional director said Nigeria currently has no active Ebola cases after the infected patient and her husband were medically evacuated out of the country. Nigerian health workers treated the patient through the acute phase of her illness before she was stabilized and flown out, with Switzerland now managing her continued care. WHO urged continued vigilance in monitoring the dozens of contacts still being tracked within Nigeria.

stories.h: Attackers kill nurse responding to Ebola case in DR Congo
stories.e: Assailants killed a nurse and wounded another health worker who were responding to an Ebola case in the Democratic Republic of Congo, underscoring the security risks facing medical teams fighting the outbreak. The attack has added to mounting concern among global health officials about containing the virus' spread across multiple African countries.

stories.h: Uganda Orders 21-Day Ebola Quarantine for Returnees From DR Congo
stories.e: Uganda has imposed a mandatory 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo as part of efforts to contain a regional Ebola outbreak. The measure comes as neighbouring countries, including Nigeria, step up surveillance and preparedness over fears the virus could spread further across the region.

stories.h: CAF reverses four-year AFCON plan, restores biennial tournament
stories.e: The Confederation of African Football has reversed its plan to move the Africa Cup of Nations to a four-year cycle, restoring the tournaments traditional two-year schedule after months of pushback from national federations and coaches. The U-turn follows a review that CAF president Patrice Motsepe launched earlier in October amid widespread opposition to the 2025 decision.

stories.h: Flamingos Edge Mexico to Reach FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Quarter-Finals
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos defeated Mexico in their Round of 16 clash at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco, with goals from Umejiaku and Dunstan sealing the win. The result sends Nigeria into the quarter-finals, where they are set to face Venezuela on Sunday. It is another strong showing for Nigerian women's youth football on the global stage at this tournament.

stories.h: Osimhen scores twice as Galatasaray beat Fenerbahce to retake Super Lig summit
stories.e: Victor Osimhen scored twice in the first half as Galatasaray beat rivals Fenerbahce 2-1 in the Istanbul derby, sending the Nigerian striker's side back to the top of Turkey's Super Lig. It's the latest strong outing in a season where Osimhen has continued to be one of the league's most prolific forwards.

stories.h: Nigeria shut out as Kane and Putellas crowned world's best at Ballon d'Or
stories.e: Harry Kane and Alexia Putellas won the men's and women's Ballon d'Or at Monday's ceremony in London, the first time the award has been handed out outside Paris. No Nigerian player made this year's shortlist, a sharp drop-off after Victor Osimhen and Ademola Lookman were in contention in recent years.

stories.h: Nigeria beat Uganda for the first time in 13 attempts to clinch T20 World Cup sub-regional qualifier
stories.e: Nigeria's cricket team finished unbeaten to top a six-nation round-robin in Abuja, beating Uganda along the way for the first time in thirteen previous meetings, and secured one of two tickets out of the sub-regional Africa qualifier. The result sends Nigeria through to the next stage of qualification for the T20 World Cup, with Uganda earning the other qualifying spot.

stories.h: Flamingos Face Mexico in FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Quarter-Final Battle
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's team, the Flamingos, are set to face Mexico as African sides push for a place in the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup quarter-finals. The match represents one of the continent's last chances to advance in the tournament.

stories.h: NPFL: Bendel Insurance End Rivers United's Unbeaten Run in Southwest Derby Stalemate
stories.e: Bendel Insurance halted league leaders Rivers United's unbeaten start to the Nigeria Premier Football League season, while a separate Southwest derby ended goalless. The results shake up the title race as the domestic season progresses.

stories.h: Iheanacho extends scoring streak as Ajayi, Awaziem shine for Nigerians abroad
stories.e: Kelechi Iheanacho scored again for Bursaspor to stretch his streak to 12 consecutive league matches, taking his season tally to 16 goals in 12 games. Semi Ajayi helped Hull City hold Premier League side Brentford to a draw and won man-of-the-match honours, while defender Chidozie Awaziem scored twice in Konyaspor's win in the Turkish league.

stories.h: Nigeria's Flamingos stun defending champions North Korea to reach U-17 Women's World Cup knockouts
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos defeated holders Korea DPR 3-1 in Morocco, with goals from Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, Oluebube Umejiaku and Kanyinsola Yusuf securing their place in the Round of 16 at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup. The win capped a mixed group stage for the young Nigerian side, who had also beaten Puerto Rico but lost to Poland.

stories.h: NFF sticks with Uyo as Super Eagles' home ground for now
stories.e: Nigeria's football federation says it is not yet ready to shift the Super Eagles' home matches to Lagos, keeping Uyo's Godswill Akpabio Stadium as the team's base for the time being. The decision follows a 3-0 home loss to Guinea-Bissau that has left Nigeria trailing in its AFCON 2027 qualifying group. Officials say Lagos' renovated Teslim Balogun Stadium is not yet cleared for international fixtures ahead of next month's qualifiers against Tanzania.

stories.h: Nigeria's Flamingos stun defending champions North Korea to reach U-17 Women's World Cup last 16
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's team, the Flamingos, beat two-time defending champions North Korea 3-1 in their final Group B match at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco, securing their place in the Round of 16 after an earlier 2-1 opening loss to Poland and a 2-0 win over Puerto Rico. Head coach Akeem Busari credited the turnaround to the squad refocusing after the Poland setback, noting it was the team's first defeat under him since he took charge in April. The result keeps alive Nigeria's bid to challenge for the title at the tournament co-hosted by Morocco.

stories.h: Flamingos stun two-time champions North Korea to reach World Cup last 16
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's team beat two-time defending champions Korea DPR 3-1 at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco, with goals from Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, Oluebube Umejiaku and Kanyinsola Yusuf sending them into the knockout round. The win capped a group stage in which Nigeria, Poland and Korea DPR all finished level on six points.

stories.h: FIFA approves normalisation committee to run Nigeria Football Federation
stories.e: FIFA has approved a normalisation committee to temporarily run the Nigeria Football Federation after its president, Ibrahim Musa Gusau, and the rest of the executive committee resigned en masse in August, derailing planned elections. The committee, to be jointly appointed by FIFA and CAF, will oversee day-to-day football administration until new elections are held, with its mandate ending no later than May 2027.

stories.h: FIFA Approves Normalisation Committee to Run Nigerian Football After NFF Mass Resignation
stories.e: FIFA's Council Bureau approved a Normalisation Committee to take over running Nigerian football after the entire NFF leadership, including president Ibrahim Musa Gusau, resigned en masse in August and derailed a planned elective congress. FIFA and CAF will jointly pick the committee's members, who are barred from contesting the eventual NFF election and must hand over power by no later than May 2027. Until then, the federation's secretariat will handle routine administration while the normalisation process unfolds.

stories.h: Lookman, Ayaosi star as Nigerian duo shine in Champions League action
stories.e: Nigerian forward Ademola Lookman came off the bench to help Atletico Madrid salvage a 1-1 draw against Stuttgart, while compatriot Emmanuel Ayaosi set up a late equaliser for Slavia Prague against Fenerbahce in this week's Champions League fixtures. Elsewhere in the competition, PSG ended Barcelona's 11-match winning run with a 4-2 victory to move top of the standings.
